body:
Phase 3 (plan §5.5): the plugin observes a running `adlc fleet` by watching `.adlc/fleet-status.json` (versioned by t-herdr-8) and reflecting the run into herdr — READ-ONLY, never seizing a worker. All decisions live in a pure, rail-tested planner; the watcher glue just executes the plan. Untrusted-input discipline from the earlier phases applies: fixed argv on the trusted PATH, ticket ids validated before they reach a path or argv, fail soft.

PROBE FIRST (record findings in the build): the exact herdr commands for (a) opening/naming a tab, (b) spawning a read-only pane running a command inside it, and (c) focusing/closing — probe the live herdr CLI and pin the argv shapes in the glue, exactly as t-herdr-2..7 did for their contracts.

WHAT TO BUILD

1. Pure planner `lib/fleet-bridge.mjs`: `planFleetBridge({ prev, curr, knownSchemaVersion, seenRunIds })` returns a plan object `{ degrade, openTab, tailPanes, notifications, boardRows }` computed with NO I/O:
   - curr null/absent (no run) -> an empty plan (degrade false, openTab null, empty arrays).
   - curr.schemaVersion is absent or !== knownSchemaVersion -> `{ degrade: true }` with empty effects (the observer must fall back to polling `fleet status --json`; the file is not trusted). Fail soft.
   - Known schema:
     - openTab: `{ runId, title: 'fleet: run-<runId>' }` when curr.runId is a non-empty string NOT in seenRunIds; else null (open once per run).
     - tailPanes: one entry `{ ticketId, state, logPath: '.adlc/fleet-logs/<ticketId>.log' }` per ticket whose state is IN-FLIGHT (building|gating|prosecuting|fixing|merging). A ticketId that is not a safe token (validated by a strict id regex — no '/', '..', leading '-') is SKIPPED (never allowed to build a log path or argv).
     - notifications: one per ticket whose state TRANSITIONED (prev !== curr) into a terminal state: to `merged` -> `{ kind:'merged', sound:'done' }`; to `failed` or `blocked` -> `{ kind, sound:'request', worktreePath: '.worktrees/fleet-<runId>' }` (carrying the open-worktree-shell target). No notification when prev already had that terminal state.
     - boardRows: one `{ ticketId, state }` per ticket currently in a terminal state (merged|failed|blocked), for the board summary.

2. Fixed-argv builders (pure, tested), using the PROBED herdr command shapes: a tab-open argv from a runId title, a read-only tail pane argv from a validated (ticketId, logPath) that runs the trusted `tail -f <logPath>` (fixed argv, no shell), a notification argv, and an open-worktree-shell argv from a validated worktreePath. Every externally-derived value is validated or `--`-separated before it becomes a positional.

3. Watcher wiring (thin glue in bin/watcher.mjs, plan §5.5): add `.adlc/fleet-status.json` to what the daemon reacts to; on appear/change, read + JSON.parse it (bounded, fail soft), call planFleetBridge with the last-seen status + seenRunIds, and execute the plan (open the tab once, spawn/refresh tail panes, fire notifications, publish board rows). On `degrade`, fall back to `fleet status --json` (or simply skip the rich UI) without error. Persisting prev-status + seenRunIds across beats is glue state.

4. Board summary: renderBoard shows a `fleet` section listing the plan's boardRows (terminal fleet tickets) when a run is present; absent otherwise. (Extend lib/board-render.mjs; do not break existing board tests.)

SECURITY (plan §6): the bridge runs UNSANDBOXED and fleet-status.json / log paths are untrusted. Ticket ids are validated against a strict token regex before forming any `.adlc/fleet-logs/<id>.log` path or argv (blocks path traversal / arg injection); every spawned command is a fixed argv of a trusted binary (`tail`, herdr) resolved on the trusted PATH; nothing derived from the status file is executed as a command; all rendered strings are sanitized; an unknown schemaVersion or malformed file degrades quietly, never crashes the daemon.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (each with a concrete verification method)

AC1 no run -> empty plan: planFleetBridge({ prev:null, curr:null, knownSchemaVersion:1, seenRunIds:new Set() }) returns degrade false, openTab null, and empty tailPanes/notifications/boardRows. VERIFY: unit test in plugins/adlc-herdr/test/fleet-bridge.test.mjs.
AC2 unknown/absent schemaVersion -> degrade: a curr with schemaVersion undefined, and one with schemaVersion 999 (!== knownSchemaVersion 1), each return `{ degrade: true }` with empty effects. VERIFY: unit tests.
AC3 new run opens a tab once: with a known-schema curr whose runId is not in seenRunIds, openTab is `{ runId, title:'fleet: run-<runId>' }`; with that runId already in seenRunIds, openTab is null. VERIFY: unit tests.
AC4 in-flight tickets -> tail panes with a safe log path: a curr with tickets in building/gating/prosecuting/fixing/merging yields one tailPane each with logPath '.adlc/fleet-logs/<id>.log' and its state; a ticket in a terminal state yields no tail pane. VERIFY: unit test asserting the tailPanes set.
AC5 malicious ticket id is skipped: a ticket id containing '/', '..', or a leading '-' produces NO tailPane and NO boardRow (never reaches a path/argv). VERIFY: unit test with hostile ids.
AC6 transitions -> notifications: a ticket going building->merged yields a merged/done notification; building->failed and building->blocked yield request-sound notifications carrying worktreePath '.worktrees/fleet-<runId>'; a ticket already merged in prev AND curr yields NO notification. VERIFY: unit tests over prev/curr pairs.
AC7 terminal tickets -> board rows: merged/failed/blocked tickets appear in boardRows; in-flight ones do not. VERIFY: unit test.
AC8 fixed-argv builders: the tail-pane argv runs `tail -f <logPath>` as a fixed argv (asserted array, no shell string), and the builders validate/`--`-guard externally-derived positionals. VERIFY: unit tests asserting the exact argv arrays.
AC9 no hollow tests: adlc hollow-test on lib/fleet-bridge.mjs (and the changed board-render) finds all mutants killed. VERIFY: preflight mutation-gate.

RAILS: plugins/adlc-herdr/test/fleet-bridge.test.mjs is frozen once authored — the executable contract for the planner, the degrade/transition/skip logic, and the fixed-argv builders.
title: herdr plugin: fleet observer bridge (run tab, tail panes, transition notifications, board summary)
